I'm triaging now (summarizing findings so far):
- Correlation: spike lines up exactly with kernel selection policy change deployed 2029-01-29T18:44:57 (last-week perf tuning).
- Observed behavior: for 32k sessions we see frequent KV-cache thrashing: large attention maps cause the runtime to evict & reload KV slices more often. When the new policy fails fast on a given GPU (due to memory/regression in kernel heuristics) it falls back to a legacy quantized kernel path that is ~4–6x slower for these large sequence lengths. That explains the p99 tail and throughput drop.
- Error causes: streaming stalls cause client timeouts which surface as 504; unrelated 500s are from a rare NPU driver transient when memory pressure surges.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (and can action now):
1) Traffic split: route CodaAI tenant to the 16k-compatible model variant (degradation for >16k tokens) — expected p99 reduction within 15–30m.
2) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for warm sessions and increase KV cache high-water threshold to avoid frequent eviction.
3) Roll back kernel selection policy to previous commit if traffic split alone doesn't stabilize within 30–60m.
4) Apply a soft per-tenant rate limit to blunt sudden bursts while we stabilize.

I attached the raw request traces (request_traces_32k.zip) — look for IDs: rq-32k-2191, rq-32k-2207.

I'll start (1) now if we have permission. ETA for visible improvement: 15–30 minutes. Full rollback & test 2–3h.

—Vivek
